1: /** Link definitions: how a label is written down, normalized, and looked up. */
2: 
3: const DEFINITION = /^\[([^\]]+)\]:\s+(\S.*)$/
4: 
5: /** One refusal of a definition, carrying the 1-based line it was read at. */
6: export class RefError extends Error {
7:   /**
8:    * @param {number} line - the 1-based input line.
9:    * @param {string} message - the message the specification words, without the position.
10:    */
11:   constructor(line, message) {
12:     super(message)
13:     this.name = 'RefError'
14:     this.line = line
15:   }
16: }
17: 
18: /**
19:  * One label in its comparable form: trimmed, whitespace runs collapsed, lowercased.
20:  * @param {string} label - the label as it was written.
21:  * @returns {string} the normalized label.
22:  */
23: export function normalizeLabel(label) {
24:   return label.trim().replace(/\s+/gu, ' ').toLowerCase()
25: }
26: 
27: /**
28:  * Read one line as a definition.
29:  * @param {string} raw - the line as written.
30:  * @returns {{label: string, url: string} | undefined} the definition, or undefined when the line is not one.
31:  */
32: export function readDefinition(raw) {
33:   const match = DEFINITION.exec(raw.trim())
34:   if (match === null) return undefined
35:   return { label: normalizeLabel(match[1]), url: match[2].trim() }
36: }
37: 
38: /**
39:  * Add one definition to a table, refusing a label it already holds.
40:  * @param {Map<string, {url: string, source: string}>} table - the definitions so far.
41:  * @param {number} line - the 1-based line the definition was read at.
42:  * @param {{label: string, url: string}} definition - the definition to add.
43:  * @param {string} source - the layer it came from.
44:  * @throws {RefError} when the label is already defined.
45:  */
46: export function define(table, line, definition, source) {
47:   if (table.has(definition.label)) throw new RefError(line, `label ${definition.label} is defined twice`)
48:   table.set(definition.label, { url: definition.url, source })
49: }

`conflayers` is the repository in this workspace: `README.md` describes what it already does, `src/` holds it, and `test/conflayers.test.js` is its own suite, which passes. Add the two layered modes its `merge` primitive was built for, make the declared types real, and report a bad value where it was written. Everything `README.md` documents about `dump`, `get`, the INI grammar and the existing failures stays exactly as it is, including every message and every column; the work spans the parser, the schema, the layer stack, and the command.

`load <base> <site>` and `origin <base> <site>` each stack three layers, weakest first: the INI file named by the first argument, the INI file named by the second, and an environment layer read from standard input. A later layer overrides a key an earlier one set, one key at a time, so a file that sets only `server.port` leaves every other key to the layer below it. The layers are read in that order, and a layer's failures are all reported before the next layer is read.

The environment layer is a line per variable. A line is trimmed first; an empty one, and one beginning with `#`, is ignored. The rest is `NAME=VALUE`: the text before the first `=` is the name, trimmed, and everything after it is the value, trimmed. A setting travels under `CONF_` followed by its key uppercased with every `.` replaced by `_`, so `server.port` arrives as `CONF_SERVER_PORT`. Its failures carry a position too, worded `error: <stdin>:<line>:<column>: ` followed by `expected NAME=VALUE` or `expected a variable name` or `unknown environment variable <NAME>` or `<NAME> is set twice`, each reported at the line's first non-space character and each counting columns the way the INI parser does.

Both modes are strict about keys where `dump` is lenient: a key an INI layer sets and the schema does not know fails with `error: <file>:<line>:<column>: unknown setting <key>` at the value's position, and a layer's keys are checked in the order the file writes them, after that file parses. The value's position is the column of its first character, or, when the value is empty, one past the line's last non-space character.

`origin <base> <site>` prints `<key> <layer>` for every schema key in ascending order, where the layer is `base`, `site`, `env`, or `default` when no layer set the key.

`load <base> <site>` prints `<key>=<value>` for every schema key in ascending order, where the value is the winning layer's text coerced by the key's declared type, or the schema default coerced the same way. A `string` is its text. An `integer` is an optional `-` and then digits without a leading zero, unless the number is exactly `0`, and renders as written. A `boolean` is `true` or `false`, lowercase, and renders as written. An `enum` is one of its declared members and renders as written. A `duration` is digits followed by `ms`, `s`, `m` or `h`, and renders as its whole number of milliseconds. A `list` is items separated by commas, each trimmed, with a repeat dropped and the order kept, rendered joined by single commas; empty text is the empty list and renders empty, but an empty item between two commas is a failure. A value that does not fit its type fails with `error: <where>: <message>`, where `<where>` is the file and position it was written at, or `<stdin>` and its position when the environment layer set it, and the message is `<key> is not an integer: <text>`, `<key> is not a boolean: <text>`, `<key> is not one of <members joined by |>: <text>`, `<key> is not a duration: <text>` or `<key> has an empty item: <text>`. The keys are coerced in ascending order, so the first failing key in that order decides.

The usage line every malformed argument list reports becomes `error: usage: cli.js dump <file>|get <file> <key>|load <base> <site>|origin <base> <site>`; `dump` takes one path, `get` a path and a key, and `load` and `origin` exactly two paths.

1: # conflayers
2: 
3: A configuration loader with no dependencies. It reads INI files, knows a fixed schema of settings, and answers what one of them is set to.
4: 
5: ## Layout
6: 
7: | File | What it owns |
8: | --- | --- |
9: | `src/cli.js` | the argument forms, the mode dispatch, and how a failure is reported |
10: | `src/ini.js` | the INI grammar and the refusals it words, as `IniError`, each with a line and a column |
11: | `src/schema.js` | `SETTINGS`, the known settings with their declared type and default text |
12: | `src/layer.js` | `merge`, which stacks layers so that the last one to set a key wins |
13: 
14: `test/conflayers.test.js` is the suite for what is already here, and `data/` holds the INI files the examples name.
15: 
16: ## The INI grammar
17: 
18: A line is trimmed first. An empty one, and one beginning with `#` or `;`, is ignored. `[name]` opens a section, and a section may be opened more than once. Anything else is `key = value`: the text before the first `=` is the key, trimmed, and everything after it is the value, trimmed. A key outside a section keeps its own name; a key inside one is prefixed with the section name and a dot, so `port` under `[server]` is `server.port`. A name and a key are one or more of the characters `A` to `Z`, `a` to `z`, `0` to `9`, `_`, `.` and `-`. Nothing inside a value is special: `#` and `;` open a comment only at the start of a line.
19: 
20: ```ini
21: log.file = /var/log/app.log
22: 
23: [server]
24: port = 9090
25: ```
26: 
27: ## The schema
28: 
29: | Key | Type | Default |
30: | --- | --- | --- |
31: | `log.file` | string | (empty) |
32: | `log.level` | enum `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` | `info` |
33: | `log.rotate` | boolean | `true` |
34: | `retry.attempts` | integer | `3` |
35: | `retry.backoff` | duration | `250ms` |
36: | `server.host` | string | `localhost` |
37: | `server.port` | integer | `8080` |
38: | `server.timeout` | duration | `30s` |
39: | `server.tls` | boolean | `false` |
40: | `tags` | list | (empty) |
41: 
42: The types are declared but nothing here enforces them yet: every mode below prints the raw text as the file wrote it.
43: 
44: ## Modes
45: 
46: - `dump <file>` prints `<key>=<raw text>` for every schema key in ascending order, falling back to the schema default for a key the file leaves out. A key the schema does not know is ignored.
47: - `get <file> <key>` prints the raw text of one setting, or its default. A key outside the schema is refused.
48: 
49: ## Failures
50: 
51: Every refusal writes one line to standard error and exits 2, having written nothing to standard output; the first failure stops the run. A grammar failure carries the position it was read at, as `error: <file>:<line>:<column>: <message>`, where the column counts characters of the raw line from 1, leading whitespace included. The messages are `expected "]"`, reported one past the line's last non-space character; `expected a section name` and `invalid section name <name>`, at the name's first character; `expected a section header or key = value` and `invalid key <key>`, at the line's first non-space character; `expected a key`, at the `=`; and `key <key> is set twice`, at the line's first non-space character. A file that cannot be read is refused as `error: cannot read <path>`, an unknown key as `error: unknown setting <key>`, and a malformed argument list with the usage line.
52: 
53: ## Known gaps
54: 
55: Only one file is ever read, so the `merge` primitive stacks a single layer and nothing overrides anything. Nothing reads the environment. The declared types do nothing: `server.port = eighty` loads as happily as `server.port = 80`, and a caller has to coerce the text itself. `IniError` carries a position, but the parse result does not, so nothing downstream could say where a bad value was written.

1: /** The settings this loader knows, their types, and the text each one defaults to. */
2: 
3: /** Every known setting, in ascending key order. */
4: export const SETTINGS = [
5:   { key: 'log.file', type: 'string', default: '' },
6:   { key: 'log.level', type: 'enum', members: ['debug', 'info', 'warn', 'error'], default: 'info' },
7:   { key: 'log.rotate', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
8:   { key: 'retry.attempts', type: 'integer', default: '3' },
9:   { key: 'retry.backoff', type: 'duration', default: '250ms' },
10:   { key: 'server.host', type: 'string', default: 'localhost' },
11:   { key: 'server.port', type: 'integer', default: '8080' },
12:   { key: 'server.timeout', type: 'duration', default: '30s' },
13:   { key: 'server.tls', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
14:   { key: 'tags', type: 'list', default: '' },
15: ]
16: 
17: const BY_KEY = new Map(SETTINGS.map(declared => [declared.key, declared]))
18: 
19: /**
20:  * The setting one key names, or undefined when the schema does not know it.
21:  * @param {string} key - the dotted setting key.
22:  * @returns {{key: string, type: string, members?: string[], default: string} | undefined} the setting.
23:  */
24: export function setting(key) {
25:   return BY_KEY.get(key)
26: }
27: 
28: const INTEGER = /^-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/
29: const DURATION = /^([0-9]+)(ms|s|m|h)$/
30: const UNIT_MS = { ms: 1, s: 1000, m: 60_000, h: 3_600_000 }
31: 
32: /** One value the schema refuses, worded without the position the caller adds. */
33: export class ValueError extends Error {
34:   /**
35:    * @param {string} message - the message the specification words, without the position.
36:    */
37:   constructor(message) {
38:     super(message)
39:     this.name = 'ValueError'
40:   }
41: }
42: 
43: /** The items of a list value, trimmed, first occurrence kept. */
44: function items(declared, text) {
45:   if (text === '') return []
46:   const out = []
47:   for (const item of text.split(',')) {
48:     const trimmed = item.trim()
49:     if (trimmed === '') throw new ValueError(`${declared.key} has an empty item: ${text}`)
50:     if (!out.includes(trimmed)) out.push(trimmed)
51:   }
52:   return out
53: }
54: 
55: /**
56:  * Coerce one setting's text and render it the way `load` prints it.
57:  * @param {{key: string, type: string, members?: string[]}} declared - the setting the text belongs to.
58:  * @param {string} text - the raw text the winning layer wrote.
59:  * @returns {string} the canonical rendering.
60:  * @throws {ValueError} when the text does not fit the declared type.
61:  */
62: export function coerce(declared, text) {
63:   switch (declared.type) {
64:     case 'integer':
65:       if (!INTEGER.test(text)) throw new ValueError(`${declared.key} is not an integer: ${text}`)
66:       return text
67:     case 'boolean':
68:       if (text !== 'true' && text !== 'false') throw new ValueError(`${declared.key} is not a boolean: ${text}`)
69:       return text
70:     case 'enum':
71:       if (!declared.members.includes(text)) {
72:         throw new ValueError(`${declared.key} is not one of ${declared.members.join('|')}: ${text}`)
73:       }
74:       return text
75:     case 'duration': {
76:       const match = DURATION.exec(text)
77:       if (match === null) throw new ValueError(`${declared.key} is not a duration: ${text}`)
78:       return String(Number(match[1]) * UNIT_MS[match[2]])
79:     }
80:     case 'list':
81:       return items(declared, text).join(',')
82:     default:
83:       return text
84:   }
85: }

1: /** The INI reader: dotted keys, the raw text of each value, and where that text sits. */
2: 
3: const NAME = /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/
4: 
5: /** One refusal of an INI line, carrying the 1-based line and column it was read at. */
6: export class IniError extends Error {
7:   /**
8:    * @param {number} line - the 1-based input line.
9:    * @param {number} column - the 1-based column of the raw line.
10:    * @param {string} message - the message the specification words, without the position.
11:    */
12:   constructor(line, column, message) {
13:     super(message)
14:     this.name = 'IniError'
15:     this.line = line
16:     this.column = column
17:   }
18: }
19: 
20: /** The 1-based column of the first non-space character of `raw`. */
21: function indent(raw) {
22:   return raw.length - raw.trimStart().length + 1
23: }
24: 
25: /**
26:  * Parse INI text into its settings.
27:  * @param {string} text - the file's whole text.
28:  * @returns {Map<string, {text: string, line: number, column: number}>} each dotted key's raw value and position, in the order the file writes them.
29:  * @throws {IniError} on the first line the grammar refuses.
30:  */
31: export function parse(text) {
32:   const lines = text.split('\n')
33:   if (lines.length > 0 && lines[lines.length - 1] === '') lines.pop()
34:   const values = new Map()
35:   let section = ''
36:   for (const [index, raw] of lines.entries()) {
37:     const line = index + 1
38:     const trimmed = raw.trim()
39:     if (trimmed === '' || trimmed.startsWith('#') || trimmed.startsWith(';')) continue
40:     if (trimmed.startsWith('[')) {
41:       if (!trimmed.endsWith(']')) throw new IniError(line, raw.trimEnd().length + 1, 'expected "]"')

24:  * The variable name one setting key travels under.

26:  * @returns {string} the variable name.
27:  */

30: }

32: /**
33:  * Parse the environment layer.

35:  * @param {readonly {key: string}[]} settings - the schema, which decides which names are known.
36:  * @returns {Map<string, {text: string, line: number, column: number}>} each dotted key's raw value and position, in the order the input writes them.
37:  * @throws {EnvError} on the first line the grammar refuses.
38:  */

40:   const lines = text.split('\n')
41:   if (lines.length > 0 && lines[lines.length - 1] === '') lines.pop()
42:   const byName = new Map(settings.map(declared => [variableName(declared.key), declared.key]))
43:   const values = new Map()
44:   for (const [index, raw] of lines.entries()) {
45:     const line = index + 1
46:     const trimmed = raw.trim()
47:     if (trimmed === '' || trimmed.startsWith('#')) continue

50:     const name = trimmed.slice(0, split).trim()
51:     if (name === '') throw new EnvError(line, indent(raw), 'expected a variable name')

8: import { coerce, SETTINGS, setting, ValueError } from './schema.js'

10: const USAGE = 'usage: cli.js dump <file>|get <file> <key>|load <base> <site>|origin <base> <site>'
11: 
12: /** Report one failure the way the specification words it, and stop. */
13: function fail(message) {
14:   process.stderr.write(`error: ${message}\n`)
15:   process.exit(2)
16: }
17: 
18: /** One INI layer, refused at its own position when the grammar or the schema rejects it. */
19: function iniLayer(name, path, strict) {
20:   if (!existsSync(path)) fail(`cannot read ${path}`)
21:   let values
22:   try {
23:     values = parseIni(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'))
24:   } catch (error) {
25:     if (!(error instanceof IniError)) throw error
26:     fail(`${path}:${error.line}:${error.column}: ${error.message}`)
27:   }
28:   if (strict) {
29:     for (const [key, value] of values) {
30:       if (setting(key) === undefined) fail(`${path}:${value.line}:${value.column}: unknown setting ${key}`)
31:     }
32:   }
33:   return { name, values }
34: }
35: 
36: /** The environment layer, refused at its own position. */

43:   }

`conflayers` is the repository in this workspace: `README.md` describes what it already does, `src/` holds it, and `test/conflayers.test.js` is its own suite, which passes. Add the two layered modes its `merge` primitive was built for, make the declared types real, and report a bad value where it was written. Everything `README.md` documents about `dump`, `get`, the INI grammar and the existing failures stays exactly as it is, including every message and every column; the work spans the parser, the schema, the layer stack, and the command.

`load <base> <site>` and `origin <base> <site>` each stack three layers, weakest first: the INI file named by the first argument, the INI file named by the second, and an environment layer read from standard input. A later layer overrides a key an earlier one set, one key at a time, so a file that sets only `server.port` leaves every other key to the layer below it. The layers are read in that order, and a layer's failures are all reported before the next layer is read.

The environment layer is a line per variable. A line is trimmed first; an empty one, and one beginning with `#`, is ignored. The rest is `NAME=VALUE`: the text before the first `=` is the name, trimmed, and everything after it is the value, trimmed. A setting travels under `CONF_` followed by its key uppercased with every `.` replaced by `_`, so `server.port` arrives as `CONF_SERVER_PORT`. Its failures carry a position too, worded `error: <stdin>:<line>:<column>: ` followed by `expected NAME=VALUE` or `expected a variable name` or `unknown environment variable <NAME>` or `<NAME> is set twice`, each reported at the line's first non-space character and each counting columns the way the INI parser does.

Both modes are strict about keys where `dump` is lenient: a key an INI layer sets and the schema does not know fails with `error: <file>:<line>:<column>: unknown setting <key>` at the value's position, and a layer's keys are checked in the order the file writes them, after that file parses. The value's position is the column of its first character, or, when the value is empty, one past the line's last non-space character.

`origin <base> <site>` prints `<key> <layer>` for every schema key in ascending order, where the layer is `base`, `site`, `env`, or `default` when no layer set the key.

`load <base> <site>` prints `<key>=<value>` for every schema key in ascending order, where the value is the winning layer's text coerced by the key's declared type, or the schema default coerced the same way. A `string` is its text. An `integer` is an optional `-` and then digits without a leading zero, unless the number is exactly `0`, and renders as written. A `boolean` is `true` or `false`, lowercase, and renders as written. An `enum` is one of its declared members and renders as written. A `duration` is digits followed by `ms`, `s`, `m` or `h`, and renders as its whole number of milliseconds. A `list` is items separated by commas, each trimmed, with a repeat dropped and the order kept, rendered joined by single commas; empty text is the empty list and renders empty, but an empty item between two commas is a failure. A value that does not fit its type fails with `error: <where>: <message>`, where `<where>` is the file and position it was written at, or `<stdin>` and its position when the environment layer set it, and the message is `<key> is not an integer: <text>`, `<key> is not a boolean: <text>`, `<key> is not one of <members joined by |>: <text>`, `<key> is not a duration: <text>` or `<key> has an empty item: <text>`. The keys are coerced in ascending order, so the first failing key in that order decides.

The usage line every malformed argument list reports becomes `error: usage: cli.js dump <file>|get <file> <key>|load <base> <site>|origin <base> <site>`; `dump` takes one path, `get` a path and a key, and `load` and `origin` exactly two paths.

1: # conflayers
2: 
3: A configuration loader with no dependencies. It reads INI files, knows a fixed schema of settings, and answers what one of them is set to.
4: 
5: ## Layout
6: 
7: | File | What it owns |
8: | --- | --- |
9: | `src/cli.js` | the argument forms, the mode dispatch, and how a failure is reported |
10: | `src/ini.js` | the INI grammar and the refusals it words, as `IniError`, each with a line and a column |
11: | `src/schema.js` | `SETTINGS`, the known settings with their declared type and default text |
12: | `src/layer.js` | `merge`, which stacks layers so that the last one to set a key wins |
13: 
14: `test/conflayers.test.js` is the suite for what is already here, and `data/` holds the INI files the examples name.
15: 
16: ## The INI grammar
17: 
18: A line is trimmed first. An empty one, and one beginning with `#` or `;`, is ignored. `[name]` opens a section, and a section may be opened more than once. Anything else is `key = value`: the text before the first `=` is the key, trimmed, and everything after it is the value, trimmed. A key outside a section keeps its own name; a key inside one is prefixed with the section name and a dot, so `port` under `[server]` is `server.port`. A name and a key are one or more of the characters `A` to `Z`, `a` to `z`, `0` to `9`, `_`, `.` and `-`. Nothing inside a value is special: `#` and `;` open a comment only at the start of a line.
19: 
20: ```ini
21: log.file = /var/log/app.log
22: 
23: [server]
24: port = 9090
25: ```
26: 
27: ## The schema
28: 
29: | Key | Type | Default |
30: | --- | --- | --- |
31: | `log.file` | string | (empty) |
32: | `log.level` | enum `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` | `info` |
33: | `log.rotate` | boolean | `true` |
34: | `retry.attempts` | integer | `3` |
35: | `retry.backoff` | duration | `250ms` |
36: | `server.host` | string | `localhost` |
37: | `server.port` | integer | `8080` |
38: | `server.timeout` | duration | `30s` |
39: | `server.tls` | boolean | `false` |
40: | `tags` | list | (empty) |
41: 
42: The types are declared but nothing here enforces them yet: every mode below prints the raw text as the file wrote it.
43: 
44: ## Modes
45: 
46: - `dump <file>` prints `<key>=<raw text>` for every schema key in ascending order, falling back to the schema default for a key the file leaves out. A key the schema does not know is ignored.
47: - `get <file> <key>` prints the raw text of one setting, or its default. A key outside the schema is refused.
48: 
49: ## Failures
50: 
51: Every refusal writes one line to standard error and exits 2, having written nothing to standard output; the first failure stops the run. A grammar failure carries the position it was read at, as `error: <file>:<line>:<column>: <message>`, where the column counts characters of the raw line from 1, leading whitespace included. The messages are `expected "]"`, reported one past the line's last non-space character; `expected a section name` and `invalid section name <name>`, at the name's first character; `expected a section header or key = value` and `invalid key <key>`, at the line's first non-space character; `expected a key`, at the `=`; and `key <key> is set twice`, at the line's first non-space character. A file that cannot be read is refused as `error: cannot read <path>`, an unknown key as `error: unknown setting <key>`, and a malformed argument list with the usage line.
52: 
53: ## Known gaps
54: 
55: Only one file is ever read, so the `merge` primitive stacks a single layer and nothing overrides anything. Nothing reads the environment. The declared types do nothing: `server.port = eighty` loads as happily as `server.port = 80`, and a caller has to coerce the text itself. `IniError` carries a position, but the parse result does not, so nothing downstream could say where a bad value was written.

1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: /** The command: `dump <file>`, `get <file> <key>`, `load <base> <site>` and `origin <base> <site>`. */
3: 
4: import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
5: import { EnvError, parse as parseEnv } from './env.js'
6: import { IniError, parse as parseIni } from './ini.js'
7: import { merge } from './layer.js'
8: import { coerce, SETTINGS, setting, ValueError } from './schema.js'
9: 
10: const USAGE = 'usage: cli.js dump <file>|get <file> <key>|load <base> <site>|origin <base> <site>'
11: 
12: /** Report one failure the way the specification words it, and stop. */
13: function fail(message) {
14:   process.stderr.write(`error: ${message}\n`)
15:   process.exit(2)
16: }
17: 
18: /** One INI layer, refused at its own position when the grammar or the schema rejects it. */
19: function iniLayer(name, path, strict) {
20:   if (!existsSync(path)) fail(`cannot read ${path}`)
21:   let values
22:   try {
23:     values = parseIni(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'))
24:   } catch (error) {
25:     if (!(error instanceof IniError)) throw error
26:     fail(`${path}:${error.line}:${error.column}: ${error.message}`)
27:   }
28:   if (strict) {
29:     for (const [key, value] of values) {
30:       if (setting(key) === undefined) fail(`${path}:${value.line}:${value.column}: unknown setting ${key}`)
31:     }
32:   }
33:   return { name, values }
34: }
35: 
36: /** The environment layer, refused at its own position. */
37: function envLayer() {
38:   try {
39:     return { name: 'env', values: parseEnv(readFileSync(0, 'utf8'), SETTINGS) }
40:   } catch (error) {
41:     if (!(error instanceof EnvError)) throw error
42:     return fail(`<stdin>:${error.line}:${error.column}: ${error.message}`)
43:   }
44: }
45: 
46: const argv = process.argv.slice(2)
47: const mode = argv[0]
48: const arity = { dump: 2, get: 3, load: 3, origin: 3 }
49: if (argv.length !== arity[mode]) fail(USAGE)
50: 
51: const out = []
52: if (mode === 'dump' || mode === 'get') {
53:   const { values } = iniLayer('file', argv[1], false)
54:   const raw = key => (values.has(key) ? values.get(key).text : setting(key).default)
55:   if (mode === 'dump') {
56:     for (const declared of SETTINGS) out.push(`${declared.key}=${raw(declared.key)}`)
57:   } else {
58:     if (setting(argv[2]) === undefined) fail(`unknown setting ${argv[2]}`)
59:     out.push(raw(argv[2]))
60:   }
61: } else {
62:   const merged = merge([iniLayer('base', argv[1], true), iniLayer('site', argv[2], true), envLayer()])
63:   const source = { base: argv[1], site: argv[2], env: '<stdin>' }
64:   for (const declared of SETTINGS) {
65:     const won = merged.get(declared.key)
66:     if (mode === 'origin') {
67:       out.push(`${declared.key} ${won === undefined ? 'default' : won.name}`)
68:       continue
69:     }
70:     if (won === undefined) {
71:       out.push(`${declared.key}=${coerce(declared, declared.default)}`)
72:       continue
73:     }
74:     try {
75:       out.push(`${declared.key}=${coerce(declared, won.text)}`)
76:     } catch (error) {
77:       if (!(error instanceof ValueError)) throw error
78:       fail(`${source[won.name]}:${won.line}:${won.column}: ${error.message}`)
79:     }
80:   }
81: }
82: process.stdout.write(out.map(line => `${line}\n`).join(''))

1: /** The settings this loader knows, their types, and the text each one defaults to. */
2: 
3: /** Every known setting, in ascending key order. */
4: export const SETTINGS = [
5:   { key: 'log.file', type: 'string', default: '' },
6:   { key: 'log.level', type: 'enum', members: ['debug', 'info', 'warn', 'error'], default: 'info' },
7:   { key: 'log.rotate', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
8:   { key: 'retry.attempts', type: 'integer', default: '3' },
9:   { key: 'retry.backoff', type: 'duration', default: '250ms' },
10:   { key: 'server.host', type: 'string', default: 'localhost' },
11:   { key: 'server.port', type: 'integer', default: '8080' },
12:   { key: 'server.timeout', type: 'duration', default: '30s' },
13:   { key: 'server.tls', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
14:   { key: 'tags', type: 'list', default: '' },
15: ]
16: 
17: const BY_KEY = new Map(SETTINGS.map(declared => [declared.key, declared]))
18: 
19: /**
20:  * The setting one key names, or undefined when the schema does not know it.
21:  * @param {string} key - the dotted setting key.
22:  * @returns {{key: string, type: string, members?: string[], default: string} | undefined} the setting.
23:  */
24: export function setting(key) {
25:   return BY_KEY.get(key)
26: }
27: 
28: const INTEGER = /^-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/
29: const DURATION = /^([0-9]+)(ms|s|m|h)$/
30: const UNIT_MS = { ms: 1, s: 1000, m: 60_000, h: 3_600_000 }
31: 
32: /** One value the schema refuses, worded without the position the caller adds. */
33: export class ValueError extends Error {
34:   /**
35:    * @param {string} message - the message the specification words, without the position.
36:    */
37:   constructor(message) {
38:     super(message)
39:     this.name = 'ValueError'
40:   }
41: }
42: 
43: /** The items of a list value, trimmed, first occurrence kept. */
44: function items(declared, text) {
45:   if (text === '') return []
46:   const out = []
47:   for (const item of text.split(',')) {
48:     const trimmed = item.trim()
49:     if (trimmed === '') throw new ValueError(`${declared.key} has an empty item: ${text}`)
50:     if (!out.includes(trimmed)) out.push(trimmed)
51:   }
52:   return out
53: }
54: 
55: /**
56:  * Coerce one setting's text and render it the way `load` prints it.
57:  * @param {{key: string, type: string, members?: string[]}} declared - the setting the text belongs to.
58:  * @param {string} text - the raw text the winning layer wrote.
59:  * @returns {string} the canonical rendering.
60:  * @throws {ValueError} when the text does not fit the declared type.
61:  */
62: export function coerce(declared, text) {
63:   switch (declared.type) {
64:     case 'integer':
65:       if (!INTEGER.test(text)) throw new ValueError(`${declared.key} is not an integer: ${text}`)
66:       return text
67:     case 'boolean':
68:       if (text !== 'true' && text !== 'false') throw new ValueError(`${declared.key} is not a boolean: ${text}`)
69:       return text
70:     case 'enum':
71:       if (!declared.members.includes(text)) {
72:         throw new ValueError(`${declared.key} is not one of ${declared.members.join('|')}: ${text}`)
73:       }
74:       return text
75:     case 'duration': {
76:       const match = DURATION.exec(text)
77:       if (match === null) throw new ValueError(`${declared.key} is not a duration: ${text}`)
78:       return String(Number(match[1]) * UNIT_MS[match[2]])
79:     }
80:     case 'list':
81:       return items(declared, text).join(',')
82:     default:
83:       return text
84:   }
85: }

1: /** The INI reader: dotted keys, the raw text of each value, and where that text sits. */
2: 
3: const NAME = /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/
4: 
5: /** One refusal of an INI line, carrying the 1-based line and column it was read at. */
6: export class IniError extends Error {
7:   /**
8:    * @param {number} line - the 1-based input line.
9:    * @param {number} column - the 1-based column of the raw line.
10:    * @param {string} message - the message the specification words, without the position.
11:    */
12:   constructor(line, column, message) {
13:     super(message)
14:     this.name = 'IniError'
15:     this.line = line
16:     this.column = column
17:   }
18: }
19: 
20: /** The 1-based column of the first non-space character of `raw`. */
21: function indent(raw) {
22:   return raw.length - raw.trimStart().length + 1
23: }
24: 
25: /**
26:  * Parse INI text into its settings.
27:  * @param {string} text - the file's whole text.
28:  * @returns {Map<string, {text: string, line: number, column: number}>} each dotted key's raw value and position, in the order the file writes them.
29:  * @throws {IniError} on the first line the grammar refuses.
30:  */
31: export function parse(text) {
32:   const lines = text.split('\n')
33:   if (lines.length > 0 && lines[lines.length - 1] === '') lines.pop()
34:   const values = new Map()
35:   let section = ''
36:   for (const [index, raw] of lines.entries()) {
37:     const line = index + 1
38:     const trimmed = raw.trim()
39:     if (trimmed === '' || trimmed.startsWith('#') || trimmed.startsWith(';')) continue
40:     if (trimmed.startsWith('[')) {
41:       if (!trimmed.endsWith(']')) throw new IniError(line, raw.trimEnd().length + 1, 'expected "]"')
42:       const name = trimmed.slice(1, -1)
43:       if (name === '') throw new IniError(line, indent(raw) + 1, 'expected a section name')
44:       if (!NAME.test(name)) throw new IniError(line, indent(raw) + 1, `invalid section name ${name}`)
45:       section = name
46:       continue
47:     }
48:     const split = trimmed.indexOf('=')
49:     if (split === -1) throw new IniError(line, indent(raw), 'expected a section header or key = value')
50:     const key = trimmed.slice(0, split).trim()
51:     if (key === '') throw new IniError(line, indent(raw) + split, 'expected a key')
52:     if (!NAME.test(key)) throw new IniError(line, indent(raw), `invalid key ${key}`)
53:     const full = section === '' ? key : `${section}.${key}`
54:     if (values.has(full)) throw new IniError(line, indent(raw), `key ${full} is set twice`)
55:     const after = raw.indexOf('=', indent(raw) - 1) + 1
56:     const rest = raw.slice(after)
57:     const column = rest.trim() === '' ? raw.trimEnd().length + 1 : after + (rest.length - rest.trimStart().length) + 1
58:     values.set(full, { text: rest.trim(), line, column })
59:   }
60:   return values
61: }

goal.objective:
`conflayers` is the repository in this workspace: `README.md` describes what it already does, `src/` holds it, and `test/conflayers.test.js` is its own suite, which passes. Add the two layered modes its `merge` primitive was built for, make the declared types real, and report a bad value where it was written. Everything `README.md` documents about `dump`, `get`, the INI grammar and the existing failures stays exactly as it is, including every message and every column; the work spans the parser, the schema, the layer stack, and the command.

`load <base> <site>` and `origin <base> <site>` each stack three layers, weakest first: the INI file named by the first argument, the INI file named by the second, and an environment layer read from standard input. A later layer overrides a key an earlier one set, one key at a time, so a file that sets only `server.port` leaves every other key to the layer below it. The layers are read in that order, and a layer's failures are all reported before the next layer is read.

The environment layer is a line per variable. A line is trimmed first; an empty one, and one beginning with `#`, is ignored. The rest is `NAME=VALUE`: the text before the first `=` is the name, trimmed, and everything after it is the value, trimmed. A setting travels under `CONF_` followed by its key uppercased with every `.` replaced by `_`, so `server.port` arrives as `CONF_SERVER_PORT`. Its failures carry a position too, worded `error: <stdin>:<line>:<column>: ` followed by `expected NAME=VALUE` or `expected a variable name` or `unknown environment variable <NAME>` or `<NAME> is set twice`, each reported at the line's first non-space character and each counting columns the way the INI parser does.

Both modes are strict about keys where `dump` is lenient: a key an INI layer sets and the schema does not know fails with `error: <file>:<line>:<column>: unknown setting <key>` at the value's position, and a layer's keys are checked in the order the file writes them, after that file parses. The value's position is the column of its first character, or, when the value is empty, one past the line's last non-space character.

`origin <base> <site>` prints `<key> <layer>` for every schema key in ascending order, where the layer is `base`, `site`, `env`, or `default` when no layer set the key.

`load <base> <site>` prints `<key>=<value>` for every schema key in ascending order, where the value is the winning layer's text coerced by the key's declared type, or the schema default coerced the same way. A `string` is its text. An `integer` is an optional `-` and then digits without a leading zero, unless the number is exactly `0`, and renders as written. A `boolean` is `true` or `false`, lowercase, and renders as written. An `enum` is one of its declared members and renders as written. A `duration` is digits followed by `ms`, `s`, `m` or `h`, and renders as its whole number of milliseconds. A `list` is items separated by commas, each trimmed, with a repeat dropped and the order kept, rendered joined by single commas; empty text is the empty list and renders empty, but an empty item between two commas is a failure. A value that does not fit its type fails with `error: <where>: <message>`, where `<where>` is the file and position it was written at, or `<stdin>` and its position when the environment layer set it, and the message is `<key> is not an integer: <text>`, `<key> is not a boolean: <text>`, `<key> is not one of <members joined by |>: <text>`, `<key> is not a duration: <text>` or `<key> has an empty item: <text>`. The keys are coerced in ascending order, so the first failing key in that order decides.

The usage line every malformed argument list reports becomes `error: usage: cli.js dump <file>|get <file> <key>|load <base> <site>|origin <base> <site>`; `dump` takes one path, `get` a path and a key, and `load` and `origin` exactly two paths.
